step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents Fyber's real-time and batch data processing pipeline for ad events. 1. Ad request events stream into Kafka and are ingested by a Spark Streaming application that writes raw Parquet files to an S3 Raw Bucket. 2. Apache Airflow triggers Spark jobs running on an Amazon EKS cluster (utilizing Spotinst for spot auto-scaling), which reads raw data from S3 and writes aggregated data into both an S3 Aggregated Bucket and Cassandra. 3. Airflow also triggers EMR to process data from the S3 Aggregated Bucket and load it into Druid for multidimensional analytics. 4. Presto queries snapshot data directly from the S3 Aggregated Bucket. 5. Finally, Cassandra, Presto, and Druid feed into the Dashboard UI to serve various query workloads (fast historical metrics, user snapshot analysis, and multi-dimensional slicing/dicing).

graph.name: Fyber Data Processing and Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Fyber processes ~15 million ad events per second. Migrating Spark workloads from Hadoop/Yarn to EKS with Spotinst achieved ~90% cost savings.
